pk.context: 200 mg oral, single dose, healthy adults

clues.kinetics: Mean absolute oral bioavailability is 79% in fasting conditions, and about 50% is bound to plasma proteins. Renal clearance of unchanged drug is 16% to 30% of the dose, and it is extensively distributed to tissues.
clues.substance: Supplied as a sulfate salt; the active moiety has a molecular weight of 335.9. A crystalline powder, freely soluble in water.
clues.product: An NDA product of 200 mg tablets sold in bottles of 60 or 100.
clues.safety: No boxed warning. Contraindicated in known hypersensitivity to closely related compounds; reported reactions include bone marrow depression and QT-interval prolongation.
clues.indication: Treatment of uncomplicated malaria and its prophylaxis, plus rheumatoid arthritis and systemic and chronic discoid lupus erythematosus in adults.
clues.mechanism: A 4-aminoquinoline antimalarial and antirheumatic agent; the mechanisms of its anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory effects are not fully known.

tell: An antimalarial and antirheumatic whose terminal half-life in whole blood is 40 to 50 days.

evidence.pk.halfLifeH: the terminal half-life ranged from 40 to 50 days in whole blood
evidence.pk.cmax: whole blood hydroxychloroquine Cmax was 129.6 ng/mL
